title: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
summary: From 13 March to 7 May 1954 Viet Minh forces under Vo Nguyen Giap besieged the French fortified garrison in the valley of Dien Bien Phu in northwestern Vietnam, led by Christian de Castries, and overran it. The defeat ended French military influence in Indochina and led into the Geneva talks, which divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel.

as_recorded.value: The battle began on March 13, 1954, and ended on May 7, 1954.
On May 7, 1954, the French garrison fell after a four month siege.

where.modern_name: Dien Bien Phu, Dien Bien Province, Vietnam
where.historical_name: Dien Bien Phu, a French-held valley fortress near the Laotian border

importance.justification: Decisive defeat that ended French rule in Indochina and set the terms for the division of Vietnam at Geneva.
